what: Australia confirms first diphtheria death amid worst outbreak in decades

clean_source_blocks.text: Australia has recorded its first diphtheria death in almost a decade as the country grapples with the worst outbreak of the vaccine-preventable disease in decades. In March, the Northern Territory (NT) declared an outbreak of diphtheria with cases also in Western Australia, South Australia and Queensland. Cases started rising in late-2025 with a sharp increase in February. This year, there have been 245 cases, marking the largest outbreak in Australia since 1991, mainly in remote Indigenous communities. On Tuesday, NT's health minister said autopsy results from an overseas lab found diphtheria was the cause of a man's death in April at Royal Darwin Hospital, the first such case since 2018. In recent weeks, the government has ramped up vaccination efforts in areas most at risk and the number of new cases was now falling, health officials said on Tuesday.

"Our government has taken this situation very seriously, and we are working hard to understand the causes and working to contain the situation," NT Health Minister Steve Edgington said. Since 30 March, there have been 10,407 vaccinations, he said. Between January last year and May this year, the NT reported 163 diphtheria cases with 48 respiratory cases and 115 cutaneous cases, which is spread via skin contact. In March, health officials in Western Australia (WA) confirmed two cases of respiratory diphtheria, the first time in more than 50 years that WA had recorded such cases. Sixty per cent of the cases this year are in the Northern Territory, followed by Western Australia with about 36%, with a few cases in South Australia and even fewer in Queensland.
Most cases are in the Northern Territory with some also in Western Australia, South Australia and Queensland.

An ongoing outbreak of a deadly disease has led to the death of an Australian for the first time since 2018. More than 140 people have been infected with the respiratory illness, diphtheria, across the Northern Territory since the start of last year. Central Australian Aboriginal Congress chief medical officer, John Boffa, told the ABC that one person had died from the disease in a remote region a number of weeks ago. Know the news with the 7NEWS app: Download today It is the first time an Australian has died from diphtheria since 2018, which according to the Australian Centre for Disease Control was an unvaccinated adult who had contracted a respiratory strain. NT Health is yet to confirm cause of death and are “awaiting results from an autopsy report about a possible diphtheria-related death”.

payload.title: Australia vahvisti ensimmäisen kurkkumätäkuoleman lähes vuosikymmeneen
payload.summary: Australiassa on vahvistettu ensimmäinen kurkkumätäkuolema sitten vuoden 2018. Maa kamppailee laajimman taudinpurkauksen kanssa vuosikymmeniin, ja suurin osa tapauksista on todettu Pohjoisterritoriossa.
payload.content:
Australiassa on vahvistettu ensimmäinen kurkkumätäkuolema lähes vuosikymmeneen, kun maa yrittää saada hallintaan vuosikymmeniin pahinta rokotteella ehkäistävän taudin purkausta. Pohjoisterritorion terveysviranomaisten mukaan huhtikuussa Royal Darwin Hospital -sairaalassa kuolleen miehen kuolinsyyksi varmistui ulkomaisessa laboratoriossa tehdyn ruumiinavauksen perusteella kurkkumätä.

## Tapaukset keskittyvät Pohjoisterritorioon

Pohjoisterritorio julisti kurkkumätäepidemian maaliskuussa. Tapauksia on todettu myös Länsi-Australiassa, Etelä-Australiassa ja Queenslandissa, mutta valtaosa tämän vuoden tartunnoista on keskittynyt Pohjoisterritorioon. Australiassa on tänä vuonna kirjattu 245 tapausta, mikä tekee tilanteesta maan suurimman kurkkumätäpurkauksen sitten vuoden 1991.

Tartuntamäärät alkoivat kasvaa loppuvuonna 2025, ja helmikuussa nousu jyrkkeni. Tauti on levinnyt erityisesti syrjäisissä alkuperäiskansojen yhteisöissä. Pohjoisterritoriossa raportoitiin viime vuoden tammikuun ja tämän vuoden toukokuun välillä 163 kurkkumätätapausta. Niistä 48 oli hengitystieinfektioita ja 115 ihon kautta leviäviä tautimuotoja.

Länsi-Australiassa vahvistettiin maaliskuussa kaksi hengitysteiden kurkkumätätapausta. Alueella kyse oli ensimmäisistä tällaisista tapauksista yli 50 vuoteen. Tämän vuoden tapauksista noin 60 prosenttia on ollut Pohjoisterritoriossa ja noin 36 prosenttia Länsi-Australiassa. Etelä-Australiassa ja Queenslandissa tapauksia on ollut vain muutamia.

## Rokotuksia on lisätty riskialueilla

Pohjoisterritorion terveysministeri Steve Edgingtonin mukaan viranomaiset ovat suhtautuneet tilanteeseen vakavasti ja pyrkineet sekä selvittämään tartuntojen syitä että rajaamaan leviämistä. Hänen mukaansa maaliskuun 30. päivän jälkeen alueella on annettu 10 407 rokotusta.

Terveysviranomaisten mukaan rokotuksia on viime viikkoina lisätty erityisesti alueilla, joilla tartuntariski on suurin. Samalla uusien tapausten määrä on alkanut laskea. Tapaus on Australian ensimmäinen vahvistettu kurkkumätäkuolema sitten vuoden 2018, jolloin kuolleen kerrottiin olleen rokottamaton aikuinen, joka oli saanut hengitysteihin liittyvän tautikannan.

Kurkkumätä on rokotteella ehkäistävä bakteeritauti, joka voi esiintyä hengitystieinfektiona tai ihon kautta leviävänä tautimuotona. Nykyisessä taudinpurkauksessa viranomaiset seuraavat sekä hengitystie- että ihotapauksia, koska ihon kautta leviävä tautimuoto on muodostanut Pohjoisterritorion ilmoitetuista tapauksista suuren osan.
summary_bullets: Australia on vahvistanut ensimmäisen kurkkumätäkuoleman sitten vuoden 2018.
Tänä vuonna maassa on todettu 245 tapausta, eniten sitten vuoden 1991.
Tapaukset keskittyvät Pohjoisterritorioon, jossa rokotuksia on lisätty riskialueilla.

Tänä vuonna maassa on todettu 245 tapausta, eniten sitten vuoden 1991.
Tapaukset keskittyvät Pohjoisterritorioon, jossa rokotuksia on lisätty riskialueilla.
article.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu toimitettuun lähdepakettiin. Kategoriaksi vaihdettu Ulkomaat, koska uutinen koskee Australiaa eikä Suomen kotimaan uutisia.
article.source_text:
Australia has recorded its first diphtheria death in almost a decade as the country grapples with the worst outbreak of the vaccine-preventable disease in decades. In March, the Northern Territory (NT) declared an outbreak of diphtheria with cases also in Western Australia, South Australia and Queensland. Cases started rising in late-2025 with a sharp increase in February. This year, there have been 245 cases, marking the largest outbreak in Australia since 1991, mainly in remote Indigenous communities. On Tuesday, NT's health minister said autopsy results from an overseas lab found diphtheria was the cause of a man's death in April at Royal Darwin Hospital, the first such case since 2018. In recent weeks, the government has ramped up vaccination efforts in areas most at risk and the number of new cases was now falling, health officials said on Tuesday.

"Our government has taken this situation very seriously, and we are working hard to understand the causes and working to contain the situation," NT Health Minister Steve Edgington said. Since 30 March, there have been 10,407 vaccinations, he said. Between January last year and May this year, the NT reported 163 diphtheria cases with 48 respiratory cases and 115 cutaneous cases, which is spread via skin contact. In March, health officials in Western Australia (WA) confirmed two cases of respiratory diphtheria, the first time in more than 50 years that WA had recorded such cases. Sixty per cent of the cases this year are in the Northern Territory, followed by Western Australia with about 36%, with a few cases in South Australia and even fewer in Queensland.

Most cases are in the Northern Territory with some also in Western Australia, South Australia and Queensland.

An ongoing outbreak of a deadly disease has led to the death of an Australian for the first time since 2018. More than 140 people have been infected with the respiratory illness, diphtheria, across the Northern Territory since the start of last year. Central Australian Aboriginal Congress chief medical officer, John Boffa, told the ABC that one person had died from the disease in a remote region a number of weeks ago. Know the news with the 7NEWS app: Download today It is the first time an Australian has died from diphtheria since 2018, which according to the Australian Centre for Disease Control was an unvaccinated adult who had contracted a respiratory strain. NT Health is yet to confirm cause of death and are “awaiting results from an autopsy report about a possible diphtheria-related death”.
